geeklist.title: MetaList for GeekList AUCTIONS
geeklist.description:
This MetaList is a current collection of Active GeekList Auctions. By posting your auction here, all subscribers will be notified of your sales.
BGG is a great avenue for finding the board games that you want. Most players take care of their games allowing for decent re-sale value. However, BGG in its current state is not an ideal place to host an auction. The community has developed a work around to make this feasible for as many people as possible. Because of the limitations, certain guidelines are needed. Please follow the rules below for all roles that are applicable to you.
[center][b][u]*** [size=15]I[/size][size=13]MPORTANT[/size] [size=15]I[/size][size=13]NSTRUCTIONS[/size] ***[/u][/b][/center]
[q][size=12][b]Instructions for Sellers:[/b][/size]
After you have created your GeekList Auction, please [b]post a single GeekList item[/b] linked directly to your auction GeekList. 1) Copy the URL of your GeekList Auction 2) At the bottom of this header, click on the white + in the blue box. 3) Paste the URL of your GeekList Auction 4) Click "Next →" 5) You may change or add an Image, by copying and pasting the Image Number (found within the URL of the image, e.g., https://boardgamegeek.com/image/[bgcolor=yellow]7596858[/bgcolor]/) 6) Click "Continue" 7) A new Item will appear on the GeekList. Please add the information listed below. 8) Confirm all information is correct [i]before [/i]clicking "✓ Save"
[size=11]Please include the following: [b]* End date[/b] (in bold or highlighted text) [b]* Any or all Items listed in the auction [/b](you may use the GeekList ImageID to highlight an item) [b]* Indicate in your own GeekList that BGG is to get their 3% commission and that your list is NOT set to private[/b] (other wise it will appear as not existing to us) [b]* Any other relevant information or special exceptions to your auction, such as... ** Shipping restrictions[/b] (US Only? Local Pick-up available?), [b]** Payment options [/b](Buy-it-Now prices? PayPal only?) [b]** Trades considered, etc.[/b]
[b][COLOR=#CC0000]Please modify the content of your GeekList Item [u]ONLY ONCE[/u] (preferably within 24 hours [i]remaining [/i]in your auction). This will notify all people that are subscribed to this MetaList.
For additional information, corrections, or reminders of end times, please only post as a [i]NEW COMMENT[/i] to your GeekList Item.
Be advised that if you break this rule, you will most likely receive GeekMail(s) reminding you of this guideline. Multiple infractions will result in your GeekList Item being deleted from the MetaList.
It is highly recommended that when you close your Auction, especially if it ends at a "random time", that you turn off Comments on your GeekList. Click on "Edit Descriptions & Header" in your Auction header. Uncheck "Allow Comments" under List Settings. This will prevent bids from coming in after the deadline. Once you record who is the high bid at the deadline, you can turn Comments back on if so desired.
Once the auction has been completed for a few days, please delete your GeekList Item on this MetaList so this MetaList can remain free of old content [i](do NOT edit it to mark it "CLOSED")[/i].[/COLOR][/b][/size]
Editing the title of YOUR GeekList to show it is closed is the best way to notify the community your Auction is closed. You should not delete your GeekList until all items have been received by bidders and any issues resolved.
If you plan on doing a follow-up auction of unsold items, you may either post a new entry (preferred) or modify the original (indicating it is a new auction in the posting). Periodically, the list will be scrubbed of auctions that have been closed for several days.
It is requested (but not required) that you link this MetaList in the comment section of your auction. This will help advertise this MetaList to the benefit of future sellers just as those that came before have helped you! This is GeekListID# 66420.
If any thing is unclear or you have a question, please contact me via GeekMail [b]prior[/b] to posting your Auction here.[/q]
[q][size=12][b]Instructions for Bidders:[/b][/size]
If you would like to be notified of new auctions, [i]please subscribe to [b]this MetaList[/b][/i].
* If you do not want to be notified of comments, you will need to modify the subscription by clicking the down arrow to the right of "Unsubscribe" in the header, then clicking on "Edit Subscription", then selecting "No" as a drop down under "Comment"; or try this link: https://boardgamegeek.com/subscription/edit/feed/geeklist/66420. ** [b]This is strongly recommended if you do not want the "noise" generated by user comments.[/b]
[COLOR=#CC0000]* Please also click the above link or "Edit Subscription" below to [b]ensure [/b]that [i]your[/i] personal default for "GeekList Item" does not resolve to "No" despite having subscribed. Otherwise you may not be notified of new auctions.[/COLOR]
* If you would like to be notified of new information of a specific auction, [i]please [u]also[/u] subscribe to [b]that specific GeekList Item[/b].[/i] This will override the general subscription setting of the MetaList. Any comment to that item will notify of the new content.
[b]* For discussion relevant to the general auction process, please comment on [thread=1901640][/thread]. For discussion relevant to a specific auction, please comment under that specific GeekList Item or within that Auction itself.[/b][/q]
[q][size=12][b]Miscellaneous Instructions:[/b][/size]
* Please only add a GeekList Item if it is [i]your[/i] auction. Sellers should have control of their own info. Instead, invite them to this thread to advertise.
* The rules included here are meant as a guideline for posting to this MetaList. For further guidelines on creating auctions, please see the wiki: https://www.boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/GeekList_auction
* Feel free to comment under any items but realize that each comment [b]will trigger all those subscribed to that item[/b]. Please keep it on point. It would be better to post any questions to the auction itself so anyone monitoring just that auction sees the discussion.
* If you want to comment on something posted under an auction that is not relevant to most subscribers (including rule infractions or discussing the infraction), [b]consider sending a polite and private GeekMail instead in order to avoid triggering a subscription notification[/b].
* As manager of this list, I reserve the right to make adjustments to the MetaList when deemed necessary. By posting on this MetaList, you are accepting these terms & conditions. [/q]

[q="ColtsFan76"]Posted above, but let's see how this goes. Perhaps we can allow a single update at the 24 hour mark. (But that would be one 24-hour notice, excluding extensions due to anti-sniping rules and such).[/q] I voted "Unlimited". My preference would be no more than once a day, to allow for the occasional necessary update. The "Once" selection doesn't cut it. Honestly, if the seller is organized, I doubt they would normally need to make multiple updates anyway.

I also voted unlimited. One edit seems too confining.
If the seller adds one of my grail games to the auction then the seller no longer has the option to warn us when there is only 24 hours left? Harsh.
Unlimited is perhaps too lax, I admit, but there has to be some leeway above one edit.
I think mcpranno is on to something with the once per day or perhaps once every two or three days with an automatic freebie at 24 hours remaining.
I just changed my vote to "unlimited." If someone is being annoying, I'll block their subscription.

[q="pmbrill77"]I also voted unlimited. One edit seems too confining.
If the seller adds one of my grail games to the auction then the seller no longer has the option to warn us when there is only 24 hours left? Harsh.
Unlimited is perhaps too lax, I admit, but there has to be some leeway above one edit.
I think mcpranno is on to something with the once per day or perhaps once every two or three days with an automatic freebie at 24 hours remaining.[/q] Again, you have the option to subscribe to the geeklist item. Each time the seller wants to update, they can post a comment, and everyone subscribed to that auction will get notification.
In addition, you can always subscribe to the auction itself, and even more importantly, to the grail item so you can monitor its progress.
The question at hand is only about updating the original entry which then triggers all those subscribed to the list, whether they care about the auction or not.
Keep in mind that we have been running around 12 current auctions at any given time (as we are moving new in and old out pretty well at this point). So if every seller updated their item once a day, that would be 12 updates a day. And when you get notification, you may have one "summary" if those were all posted since the last time you checked in, or you may have up to 12 updates throughout the day. That is what gets annoying and makes people unsubscribe. And that ultimately will kill the list.
So I don't think a single edit list-wide is too limiting as everyone still has the ability to do comment updates.
I's like to wait until we have at least 100 polled (since we have just over 100 thumbs) before making the final decision, but it looks like one edit at the 24 hour mark is the consensus.

Is there a consensus on whether and when to lock the old thread (perhaps after making one more post) or do away with this geeklist? I think the instructions to post auctions here are getting buried in the thread, which illustrates one of Gerry's points for using a geeklist in the first place:

I think the instructions to post auctions here are getting buried in the thread.[/q] Octavian is willing to lock it but I asked for him to hold off until we knew this was working. I am still subscribed to the old thread and do periodic searches on geeklists anyway and invite all sellers here.
So besides those couple who just don't want to post here for whatever reason, I think we have all the auctions listed here. Every couple days I am deleting old closed ones. So I think this is working as intended.
Once an auction is done does it get removed from this list?

[q="corkysru"]Once an auction is done does it get removed from this list?[/q] Yes. The seller is encouraged to do it on his own. But if not, I will do it after a set amount of days.
I am still debating when the best time is and so far doing after 5 days (after reducing that from a week). The reason I am not doing it immediately is severalfold:
1) I am not sure if some auctions have anti-sniping rules that are extending it a few days
2) The seller may want to repost a new auction with items left over and has the opportunity to just change the original post (though I recommend a new entry).
3) Some people may want a quick link to just completed auctions in order to track payment/shipping.
4) Some people may just want to follow up on what closing prices were, can't remember where they saw an item of interest, or whatever historical reason they may want.
I like that we are down on one page so if closed auctions start pushing us into a 2nd page, I may delete them a bit earlier.

How does this list interact with the Geeklist Auction Subscription Thread? http://www.boardgamegeek.com/thread/376624/geeklist-auction-subscription-thread/new
Does a buyer need to subscribe to both? Does a seller need to post in both places? Is the thread obsolete?

They do not interact with one another. The way I understand it is some are hoping this geeklist should replace the previous thread (376624).
However, many people are posting on both since not everyone is subscribed to this one (or some prefer the thread over the geeklist). I suspect that will continue since sellers want to attract as many folks as they can

[q="belial1134"]They do not interact with one another. The way I understand it is some are hoping this geeklist should replace the previous thread (376624).[/q] That is basically it.
However, if you post there first, I will notify you of this geeklist. When we feel this list is the best route to go, the old thread will be shut down.

For those new sellers that have posted recently, please make sure the following is in your Item listing here:
1) END DATE in bold font.
2) Make sure the link to your auction works. You can use a board game picture of your choice to highlight your best item, but do not use that board game as the item or no one can get there.
3) Please list a couple of the items so potential bidders can quickly gauge if they want to stop in.
4) List any special restrictions, such as PayPal only. Also list if the auction is limited to just the US or your specific country. We are an international community.
5) Etiquette is to only edit your item once with only 24 hours to go to your auction's close. However, most here are accepting that if you have a major snafu, that you can correct it immediately after posting to fix it. But if you do, make sure you have everything above so you won't have to edit it again.
Any questions, refer to the header of this geeklist at the top of any page. You can also geekmail me questions if you need assistance.
I also recommend putting the end date in the Geeklist title. That is very helpful.

Anecdotes aside:
This isn't eBay. It's a tighter community of fellow game enthusiasts (and the auction mechanism isn't automatic*). Treating them like morons isn't nice. And I guarantee that in most cases, if they're on this site, their English is better than the average American's any-other-language.
And speaking as someone who pays higher than average postage on games on a regular basis, it's not a surprise to most of us that we will pay more (sometimes a lot more) to get things in the mail. But that's our choice to make, so don't restrict shipping because [b]you[/b] think it's too much. If you don't want to deal with customs forms, if you're afraid of long-distance insurance claims, if you just don't want your games to leave the lower 48, that's fine; go ahead and restrict your auction to US addresses only.
But try to be polite about it. "US addresses only please" is almost perfect ("Sorry, US addresses only, please" would be perfect).
"Any items won by international winners will go to the next US bidder." says "I think you foreigners are dumb. And I will not try to help you out if you make a mistake, I will ignore your existence." It also says "I'm not really paying attention to my auction until the end," but I guess that's an auction-giver's prerogative.
* Hint to xenophobic eBay auctioneers: you can restrict your auctions so that foreigners [b]can't[/b] bid, if you set it up properly.

While I agree with you on the average boardgame geek being better in English by virtue of the site...and most of the 'jerks' I've dealt with have all been Americans (there have been some folks I've dealt with on here that definitely qualify as 'piece of work' but not quote 'a-hole'), I do take some offense to being insinuated as a xenophobic ebayer.
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenophobia Xenophobia is defined as "an unreasonable fear or hatred of foreigners or strangers or of that which is foreign or strange".
[i]I don't think it's irrational when it costs me.[/i] What if that guy from Mexico had won? I would have had to pay the final value fees. Then I would have had to talk to customer support to ask for a refund. Then relisting the auction for another week. Horrible? No. Inconvenient enough to bitch about it on boardgamegeek? YES.

I don't doubt there can be problems, but again, this isn't eBay.
As for restricting eBay auctions, look here:
[url]http://thebrewsnews.wordpress.com/2008/06/12/ebay-sellers-can-restrict-buyers-by-adding-bidder-requirements-to-listings/[/url]
The important part for you is this:
[q]Buyers in countries to which I don’t ship
Using this buyer requirement block is especially important if you ship domestically only. A seller who does not offer their items internationally will want to block all buyers who live outside their country. Note that once again you can always exempt buyers on a case-by-case basis.[/q]
You won't have problems if non-domestic bidders can't physically bid.
Note: I was using "xenophobic" in a hyperbolic manner. I'm certain that most people don't actually hate or fear foreigners, just the hassles of international shipping. But still, please be polite. :)

This is just my experience from my geeklist auctions (and this is in no way bringing down what you say because I would like to pay the least amount of shipping as possible as well).
I try to make sure that I charge the least amount on shipping so I have standard priority mailboxes on hand and weigh the game plus the box and verify what it is going to cost through USPS.com. If the amount is less than a flat rate box, I use the lesser amount. If not, I use the flat rate box.
People use the flat rate boxes simply because of ease. No weighing; no figuring anything else out; no waiting in line at the post office; just go out to the internet and print a shipping label and go.
Some people don't have scales in their house to figure out the weight of boxes easily at home so that means a trip to the post office.
Add in to that:
- Some buyers want it shipped parcel post which that shipping label can't be printed off online so to the post office the person has to go.
- Even after you figure out shipping and go through the work of ensuring that you are giving the lowest cost, some buyers still don't like the shipping costs and that turns into an interesting conversation.
- Sometimes it is also easier to know the shipping costs up front versus waiting to get an address to calculate shipping. Buyers pay via paypal and don't include the shipping costs and then the seller is chasing down the buyer to get those costs. The seller then says they never got the shipping costs even though they were in the marketplace transaction and around and around people go.
I truly do understand that all buyers want to pay the least amount on shipping costs. I am the same way. It just depends on the amount of work that the seller really wants to do and that is the risk the seller takes.

I'll just add that you can print parcel post (or first class, or media mail) postage in PayPal when someone pays you there. You can then drop it off at the post office without standing in line.
This is how it works when I do an auction (I have a scale that I got off of ebay for about $16, and it has paid for itself many times over):
When someone buys something, I bundle it and put it in a box (not taped, if it will fit in several kinds of boxes, such as flat rate vs. non). If it's a few ounces from going up to the next pound and I know I'll need packing materials, I round up. I enter the dimensions, weight, and zip code at USPS.com. If it's one game and reasonably near by, Priority Mail with free delivery confirmation and online discount is often the cheapest. If it's heavy or far away, I geekmail the person with the options (say, $12.42 for Parcel Post, $13.85 for Priority). They choose, pay me all at once, and I send it out.

An "issue" transpired over the last couple of days that I want to address.
This is in no way meant to continue the discussion itself or to be perceived as public chastisement of the seller. The two of us have discussed the situation privately and I confident we have an understanding of each other's position and are working to reintroduce the auctions for the benefit of everyone.
I was a bit taken aback by some comments directed at me and my handling of the matter. This is the motivation for this post.
My concern was with the posting of multiple auctions by the same seller within a short period of time all ending on the same date. Given the announcement that one thousand games were to be listed, but only 25 appeared on each list, I had visions of 40+ new auctions flooding the MetaList in a very short period of time.
I choose to make this a public announcement for two reasons. One, I am fed up with the constant bickering about subscription notifications. I look at both sides in this and get frustrated with the same arguments that flare up over and over again. It has made this "labor of love" for the past 13 months more labor than love recently. So I was hoping by posting publicly this would nip yet another discussion in the bud. It was my way of saying "I am on it, please leave it alone."
Two, I did it for the same reason that all of the watch dogs post publicly - to convince others to NOT do the same thing. What I thought I saw was a side step around the rules. While no rule was broken, it seemed the spirit of the rule was broken (I understand now that was not the intent). I did not want this to open up a new round of debate or for others to find a potential loophole to the "one item, one edit" rule.
I don't like playing the trump card that this is my list and I will do what I want. But it is my "service" to this aspect of the community and I feel I have the right to take on issues or apparent rule violations that I see to keep this list as efficient as possible. As such, I have taken the opportunity to revise the header yet again to make some clarifications and reserve the right to make changes that I deem necessary.
Finally, I am not posting this to continue the discussion (as I said at the beginning) nor am I looking for any accolades. In essence, I don't want another discussion flaring up to clog up the subscription line again. But I felt strongly enough to post this. If you want to discuss it further, send me a GeekMail.
Thanks for your time.
-brian

I really don't think "soft reserve" means what many (most?) sellers think it means.
:shake: to the sellers that list prices with "soft reserve" yet, if the bids are $1 or $2 below that, won't sell.
Maybe just call it what it is going forward, which is a "reserve"?

[q="eapeas"]I really don't think "soft reserve" means what many (most?) sellers think it means.
:shake: to the sellers that list prices with "soft reserve" yet, if the bids are $1 or $2 below that, won't sell.
Maybe just call it what it is going forward, which is a "reserve"?[/q]
They're not using the wrong term just because they didn't accept a bid that was close. By definition a soft reserve means that a seller [i]might[/i] consider a lower price. Key word there is "might".
There are lots of reasons why a seller might accept one bid that is $10 less than their soft reserve and decline another offer that is just $2 short.
If somebody absolutely wants a game and will be upset if their under-bid of a few bucks is declined then they need to pony up the extra dollar or two to meet the soft reserve.

Having bought over 100 games from BGG auctions in the last 3 months, Id think that I have enough experience in these to speak knowledgeably about the "soft reserve" issue.

[q="eapeas"]Having bought over 100 games from BGG auctions in the last 3 months, Id think that I have enough experience in these to speak knowledgeably about the "soft reserve" issue.[/q] Soft reserves are conditional. Doesn't mean they have to accept anything lower... but they MIGHT.
Minimum bids.. they will NOT accept anything lower.
The difference between Hard reserves and minimum bids on the other hand is confusing.

a soft reserve can be harder or softer depending on many individual reasons. For an auction I did recently, I accepted some bids below soft reserves on some games, while I did not accept bids below soft reserves on other games. The reasons I accepted the low bids included
1) I really didn't like the game and wanted to see it go 2) The buyer bought other stuff 3) The buyer pointed out my soft reserve might be too high - and was correct. 4) The buyer was local so I wouldn't have to ship
The reasons I did not accept a low bid were ...
1) I didn't mind holding onto the game 2) The bid came in just under the wire 3) The buyer was only buying one thing 4) I got a different offer after the close of the auction and accepted it
I had one person not buy the one game he won because I didn't accept his lower than soft reserve bid on another - not a huge deal but I wish he would have bailed BEFORE he said he'd buy it in the market, and then never cancel it despite asking him too - but that's the way it goes.
Every sellers list of reasons will be different of course, but those were mine that I can recall off the top of my head. I've been on the other side too, where my near but below soft reserve was not accepted for various reasons.

I wouldn't have jumped on it so quickly if I didn't see that others have also had issues with this user.

1) Have you tried changing your subscription to only send notifications with geeklist items only (i.e. not comments)?
If you go to your subscriptions page, you should be able to change your subscriptions notifications by clicking the little down triangle besides the name on the list (or by the unsubscribe link).
If there are no pending notifications in your list, you'll need to click the 'manage subscriptions' tab on the top, and then the 'geeklists' tab beneath it to get this (or you could just wait until there is a notification in your subscriptions).
Once you've clicked that triangle, you'll see an option to edit subscriptions. Clicking on that brings you to the two options on what triggers your subscription notification. Change the default yes on the comments to no.
This will drop the number of times your subscription triggers.
2) As for the next new item - you can always click the little green arrow to the right of the page numbers at the top/bottom right corner of the list, or the the bottom right of the entire page. This will send you to the next thing that triggers your subscription. Otherwise, AFAIK, you'll have to scroll through the page and look out for the red blocks to see what has changed on the individual page. This is an overall BGG system issue though - posting a complaint here about it won't help as there is nothing anyone running or following this list can do about it.
Edit: You could also subscribe to this thread instead, although it isn't as complete or as useful as this list: [thread=376624][/thread]

I'm been using this list since Brian created it and all this time I am under the following assumptions that these are the rules/guidelines. I may be wrong, but here goes:
1. Add your geeklist to this item preferably with your geeklist as the title for the benefit of the auction aggregator, but that's not mandatory
2. You are allowed to edit your geeklist item once, typically used in the last 24 hours of your auction
3. If you have additions, subtractions, corrections, etc that you wish to make to your geeklist item, do it by adding your note as a comment to your item and not by editing it. I have never seen any rules as to how many times you may add a comment to your geeklist item. The only times I can recall this being an issue is when a lengthy discussion/argument (for whatever reasons) started. If the seller made 3 legit comments (added some games, had to remove a game, had to extend the deadline) then I don't believe that is abusing the system even if it was 3 or perhaps more comments adding more games - they are relevant notices to the auction. I'm not sure if someone did 3 comments - a 72 hr, 48 hr, and 24 hr reminder - would even be technically against the rules. It might be looked upon as annoying and bad taste but doesn't seem to be directly violating laid out rules
4. When your auction is over, edit the title of your geeklist auction with 'Closed', do not edit your geeklist item on this Metalist
5. You may leave your geeklist item on this page for a couple of days after your auction is over. Then you can delete it or Brian will do so when he cleans up the list. From what I can tell, he doesn't mind removing your closed auctions from this list :) but obviously it's nice to remove it yourself.
Those are the 5 main rules that I follow. I think, and I could be wrong, that: 6. If your geeklist auction has only BINs it is not considered an auction and therefore should not be posted to this list

I've had numerous sellers not go through the marketplace because they said they do it all as one lump amount at the end. Usually it is with people who are selling a lot of items but are not all storefront sellers (I've only bought from one big storefront seller on here and that person did it but way more than one private sellers did it the same way). If someone is selling dozens of items, a hundred-plus items, it is easier for them to do it as one big listing rather than create and confirm dozens of marketplace listings for all items sold. I'll ask while messaging them my address (if they didn't already create a listing and direct me to it) how they are handling it and if they say they create one big listing for everything sold and take care of the BGG fees that way, I'm cool with it because I am not going to automatically assume they are lying. I personally insist all buyers go through the marketplace when buying games in my auctions for a few reasons -
1) it gives me one place to look for everyone's shipping address 2) it helps me keep track of where things are 3) it gives me an easy way to create an 'invoice' and send payment instructions 4) it allows me to give feedback to the users, and vice versa 5) it allows the sales statistics to have more data 6) with the create marketplace quick link it's easy to create and will even notify the buyer that it is there
For me, if they don't 'buy' the stuff in the marketplace, they're not getting the game shipped out (:
My last auction had 200 items, with around 170 items selling - even with big auctions, I feel the effort to do individual marketplace transactions is justified.

In the good old days, the USPS was mandated to break even overall. In those days, standard mail (junk mail) subsidized a lot of other rates.
Then Congress got involved. Changed the regulation so that every rate type had to pay for itself. That led to the soaring first class rates, which pushed more folks out of mailing, which led to higher rates, which pushed more people out...etc.
Thanks Congress!

I would say it is the opposite problem. Auctions need to return to 1 week on average. Sellers seem to think longer auctions equal more bids and I think it is the opposite. When auctions were going up for only 1 week, people tended to ignore items if they went over the one week mark. Why bid on something I have no idea I might win in a month, when any number of auctions may come up within that time and close.
Much like Kickstarter, most activity is when it first goes up and int he final hours. A longer campaign might get you a little more exposure but it isn't going to drastically improve sales.
Being on the first page isn't really a special status. the main trigger is the auction aggregator and the subscriptions. As mentioned above, most people probably gloss over page 1 anyway. I typically only focus on the most recent (i.e. last) page. I only go to the first page when clearing out the closed auctions.

[u][b]Tips for the sellers:[/b][/u]
1) [b]Put your city and state in the title or in the first line of the post on this thread[/b] if a local pick-up is possible. [b]Why:[/b] Local pickups are great and result in higher final prices but far too often people need to go to the auction thread and read through the entire auction description to find out if you are located nearby or on the other side of the country. Put city + state rather than a zip code because zip codes often need to be Googled to see where they are, whereas city + state are instantly obvious.
2) [b]Put a complete list of your games in the post on this thread[/b]. [b]Why:[/b] It is so much easier to quickly scan or CTRL+F search if the titles are right here in this thread rather than having to click to individual auctions and going through pages to find out what you even have for sale. With so many auctions available, going through each of them is very time consuming.

[q="infi01"]Local pickups are great and result in higher final prices [/q] This is purely speculative. Depends on a lot of factors like the game itself and if any local buyers have interest. All the stars need to align to make that statement true.
[q="infi01"]rather than having to click to individual auctions and going through pages to find out what you even have for sale.[/q] This is a completely unnecessary convenience to potential buyers and is [b]BAD[/b] for a seller. Sellers want potential buyers to browse their entire geeklist and not just a quick window shopping drive-by.

[q="peteyboy100"]Do we know what percentage of winning bidders flake out once they figure out shipping is generally >$10? Are there other shipping option I don't know about? [/q]

Why does work address make a difference?

[q="aceves_andrew"]Why does work address make a difference?[/q] Businesses often have regular pickups and/or deliveries along existing delivery routes. Residential addresses often stray from those routes.
[q="aceves_andrew"]Why does work address make a difference?[/q] There is a business to business discount.
Hmmm that's very interesting! Is there a big difference in the discount? I can't wait to try this out!

[q="aceves_andrew"]Hmmm that's very interesting! Is there a big difference in the discount? I can't wait to try this out![/q]
Unless I'm mistaken (and I did work in shipping and receiving for a number of years, and my wife currently does), businesses, even small businesses, can negotiate with FedEx or UPS for a business discount to ship [i]anywhere,[/i] including residential. So if you can get your boss to let you ship something out through the business system, and pay it back in cash, you can oftentimes ship something to any FedEx/UPS deliverable address for [u]very[/u] cheap. Whether or not you can has to do with how your company handle its accounting for shipping/receiving. Plus, ya know, company rules and stuff.
As for shipping from a drop-off location/scheduled pickup to a business, I think you save money because you're using FedEx/UPS Ground. So, like Chris said, because the "Ground" routes move a very large number of deliveries along certain regular shipping routes, it costs them less to ship your package. When you deliver to residential addresses you're using the FedEx/UPS Home Delivery program, which is more expensive that "Ground." Because the trucks have to go out of their way to deliver to your doorstep.
edit: Both ways, delivering to a company or delivering from a company can mean a substantial discount. The difference in FedEx/UPS being more expensive than USPS to being cheaper than USPS.

I've had a small number of bidding experiences turn sour for me. One time I bid on an item that had a soft reserve. I bid the soft reserve and was not outbid when it had long-passed the time that the auction should be over. The seller never posted again or marked the auction closed and time passed, so I messaged them asking if the auction was closed and what the status of the item was. The seller responded that the auction was over with no winning bids. I said "Oh, okay. The soft reserve for that item was $X.XX and I bid $X.XX, so I thought I had won it." A week went by without hearing anything, so I messaged again with a bit of snark and said that I guessed they weren't intending on selling it? The seller said that they didn't accept the offer made at the soft-reserve price. I was like "Ummm, that isn't how soft-reserves work."
Another time, an auction had a rolling ten minute stop time at the end where every new bid added ten minutes and the item would be sold when the item went ten minutes with no bids. Another bidder and I were going back and forth bidding and extending the time and the seller ended the auction after one of the bids before ten minutes had passed, in the other seller's favor. I pointed it out immediately that item should still be live and rather than saying "Oh, my bad; I can't tell time. Let the auction continue," he was just like "Oops. Other seller still wins though."
Hope you get the game you want.

[q="ErikBoard"]I have no problem with people adding their city if they want to, but the end date is far more important in my opinion. If someone is only interested in local pick-ups, then they only have to check the location of an auction once. However, if you have bid on an item, it is very useful to be able to see the end date in your subscription. If I see that an item I bid on has the auction ending today, I am going to go check if I am still winning the bid. If there is no date, I might not remember when it ends and not realize in time that I was outbid. This hurts sellers (missing out on chance to bid again) and hurts buyers (more bidding = more money).
Edit: Also useful for items you are considering even if you haven't bid. For example, I have around 10 items I am vaguely interested in, but only a few have the end date in the title. For those without an end date, I don't intend to keep checking them to see the end date. For those with an end date, I will click on them the day before or day of the end date and decide to bid or not depending on if my interest has piqued and what is the current bid. I auppose I'll chime in, too...but not with an opinion, but rather to educate.
For those who like posting pictures, here's how to put them in a line instead of listing vertically:
When choosing the image, add the word 'inline' after the picture's ImageID. Do this for each picture, and as long as it fits, it will show the picture 'in a line'....self-explanatory.
So for example, this: [ImageID=4609315 large]
Looks like this: [ImageID=149717inline][ImageID=133832inline][ImageID=30870inline]

Picture-less lists are my favorite. I don't recognize a lot of game boxes, and at least text is a lot smaller than pictures. Discovery of new titles is easier with text titles as well, since they're easier to read at a glance.
It's a nice compromise between providing lots of info up-front and requiring tons of scrolling.

[q="OgieOgilthorpe2"]Is there a place to go, where I can see what items I am bidding on across all auctions?[/q]
When I bid on an item in an auction, I always subscribe to that GeekList item. Then you can go to your subscriptions and filter by geeklist items to see items for which you have placed bids.

I'm in the habit of making my bids like this:
$50 - 80204 - The name of the game
(Where 80204 is my zip code)
This when when I'm reviewing the geeklist item comments, I can see what I've bid on what. (The zip code is because a number of sellers like you to provide your zip code with the bid, and it's easier to just always do it the same way.)
If the bidding gets particularly heated, I start making jokes on the name when I do my bids, for fun, because I'm less likely to forget what I bid on. So, "Nameless Campaign" may become "Nameless Camping" or "Gnomeless Campaign" or whichever. :)

[q="BrokenAxe"][q="Madcapmartini"]Apologies in advance, this is likely not the best place to ask this, but I'm at a loss.
In the past, once an auction ended, there was an automated system for contacting buyers, and sending/receiving payment, shipping, and address notifications.
I've marked my items as sold, but my buyers and I cannot figure out how to proceed. Am I expected to manage each transaction manually?[/q] Unfortunately, you have to message everyone individually.[/q] That's ridiculous!
Sorry. But . . . why?! How is this an improvement?!
Thanks for your response.
It's not really an improvement. It's a result of the new systems and how the BGG Market works after the overhaul

[q="gutteranthems"]It's not really an improvement. It's a result of the new systems and how the BGG Market works after the overhaul[/q]
And after federal meddling

Well, from what I understand, the business that ran the platform that BGG moved to was a start up that failed and went out of business. A decision was made to not move back to the old system but to basically have sellers manage everything themselves and BGG just becomes a posting board more or less. I suspect this is to pre-emptively defend against potential liability related to seller behavior and BGG's implicit responsibility for vetting sellers on their platform, which they aren't really equipped to do. By becoming just a place to post sales instead of a platform for managing sales, they limit their liability. Welcome to the US, the most litigious country in the world!!

Generally comments/chat on this list is discouraged, there's a general discussion thread Brian links to and other forums if you want to chat about BGG changes.

item.objectname: "MetaList for GeekList AUCTIONS" Rules and Discussion Page
item.body:
[size=14]Public Service Announcement:[/size]
It is necessary to amend the rules of the MetaList for GeekList AUCTIONS. Due to the ongoing subscription notifications, I am reluctant to make modifications. Instead, I am going to maintain the official rules on this thread ([thread=1901640][/thread]) and link the following posts in the header. The main header will probably have some tl;dr rules with instruction to go to the thread for the full rules.
In addition, this will now also be the home for any and all discussion in regards to the MetaList. If there are any questions about the MetaList in general, application of rules, reporting of rules violations, suggested updates, it should be posted in the thread. Any comments for specific auctions can be directed under those entries, though I hope those remain at a minimum.
The first several posts are the current rules broken down by category. Updates will be a work in progress over the next few weeks. Once I feel they are ready enough to go live, I'll make a final edit to the header above, link to the thread and clean up the header. In the meantime, feel free to make any rule modification suggestions in the thread.
Probably the most needed update is the Auction Aggregator link and what, if anything, should replace it.
I'll let this entry cycle through the MetaList and remove it sometime after it has made its way to the top.

item.objectname: DixiJos monthly charity auction (Free worldwide shipping) - Ongoing Auction-List. Closed and sold items included
item.body:
I am running a monthly charity auction.
Every month I am listing at least one game.
The money raised by the auction, will every month be donated to a different help organization.
Aim of the geeklist is to put different help organizations into spotlight and encourage fellow geeks to donate for the good cause.
Running time: [b]Auctions start on the [b]first of the particular month[/b] and ends on [b]the last of the same month.[/b][/b]
Every listed game comes with [b]free worldwide shipping.[/b]
There is [b]no reserve[/b] on the items.
Won items can be paid by bank transfer, paypal or amazon.de gift voucher.
The complete amount raised by the auctions will go to the help organizations. Shipping costs and BGG fees are on me.
Geeklist Items so far:
- June 2014 [thing=107529][/thing] - July 2014 [thing=115][/thing] - August 2014 [thing=37907][/thing] to raise money for Ingenieure ohne Grenzen
[size=18]Please spread the word and join in bidding.[/size]

item.body:
[center] [size=18]🌳 [b]Trees planted: 1772[/b] 🌳 🎋 [b]Projects supported: 12[/b] 🎋[/size][/center][hr]Hi. I'm Alex.
I'm splitting every buck I make from board games with our world by donating 50% of all [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/market/user/ZombieBoard][b]sales[/b][/url] and [url=https://ko-fi.com/zombieboard][b]donations[/b][/url] to a tree-planting charity. This geeklist is another way to generate more tree money and raise awareness of our planet's basic needs. Why 50% and not 100%? The remaining 50% will be used to acquire more games. More games mean more auctions, more trees planted, and more awareness in a hopeful, ever-bigger snowball of future saplings.
Here are the [b]rules of the game[/b]:
🌱 One game, or bundle, for auction around the start of the month until the last day (GMT time zone). 🌱 In the item's description, I'll spotlight the location in the world, which will receive 50% of the money raised to plant trees, through tree planting organizations. 🌱 I'll set up a Geekmarket sale for BGG's 3%. 🌱 [b][u]Free shipping worldwide is on me[/u][/b].

item.objectname: They are Just Sitting on a shelf Auction!
item.body:
[b]Shipping from 44004. BGG will get their 3% through the sell function of the geek list.[/b] [b]Auction will end sometime in the evening/Night of the February 6, 2026. I Will not specify a time to avoid sniping. [/b]If you wish to make a bundle deal I will listen to offers.
[b]Please make sure everything is paid within 24 hours as I have Monday to ship. [/b]That's the only day I have for Post Office runs.
I will only accept the SB as the lowest price. All Games are retail unless otherwise stated. If I have to ship to the west coast I will get the shipping as low as I can but if the item(s) are heavy please understand it won't be super cheap.
[b]I will accept PayPal, Venmo. I will combine shipping on multiple items. I will Use Pirate ship or Paypal ship station which offers the same rates. Please make sure your Paypal address is the address you live at.[/b]
If you want pictures of anything message me your Phone number I will send any pics you want.
[b]The More you buy the Cheaper Shipping is! Get 1 dollar off shipping for each Item you buy![/b]
Thank you all the Board Gaming Community is Awesome!
Games Included but not everything...
Zombicide Green Horde with 2 expansions Lightning Train Comic Hunters Concordia Critter Kitchen Darkest dungeon plus Kickstarter extras and expansions. Everdell Farshore Fox Experiment Wooden edition FrostPunk plus accessories expansions All 3 South Tigris Base games LOTR: Fate of the Fellowship Luthier Wooden Worker chips March of the Ants: Evolved edition. Mind MGMT River Valley Glassworks Deluxe Tea Garden Unconscious Mind Werewolf in the Dark
And much much More!!!
